What is the reference period or as-of date on the prevalence of low HDL-C in adults age 20 and older during August 2021–August 2023 (crude)?
response_text:
**Reference period: August 2021–August 2023** — the NHANES data collection cycle, not a single as-of date.

The crude prevalence figure (13.8%, 95% CI 12.1–15.7, SE 0.8, n = 5,498) is a period estimate pooled across the full ~2-year continuous survey cycle. NHANES has no point-in-time reference date; examinations were conducted continuously across that window, and the estimate describes the civilian noninstitutionalized U.S. population age 20+ over the period as a whole.

Two things worth noting alongside it:
- **Crude vs. age-adjusted**: 13.8% is the unadjusted estimate for the actual 2021–2023 population; the age-adjusted counterpart (14.2%) standardizes to the 2000 U.S. census population and is the one to use for comparison across cycles.
- **Cycle irregularity**: this cycle runs August 2021–August 2023 rather than the usual 2-calendar-year format because NHANES field operations were suspended in March 2020 due to COVID-19; the partial 2019–March 2020 data were released separately as a nationally representative "2017–March 2020 prepandemic" file. So this cycle is not directly interchangeable with the pre-2020 2-year cycles for trend purposes without care.
